source.text: Καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖν· Ἀμπελῶνα ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν, καὶ περιέθηκεν φραγμὸν καὶ ὤρυξεν ὑπολήνιον καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.

records.literal_gloss: And he began to them in parables to speak: A vineyard a man planted, and placed around [it] a fence, and dug a wine vat, and built a tower, and rented out it to farmers, and went abroad.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to speak to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard, and put a fence around [it], and dug a vat under the winepress, and built a tower, and leased it out to tenant farmers, and went abroad.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach them in parables. "There was a man who planted a vineyard and put a hedge around it. He dug a vat below the winepress and built a lookout tower. Then he leased the vineyard to tenant farmers and went to another country.
en.R: Jesus began to teach them with word pictures. "There was a man who planted grapevines in a field. He built a fence around it. He cut a pit in the rock to catch the juice when the grapes were pressed. He built a tower where a guard could watch over the vines. Then he rented the vineyard to some farmers, and he went on a long trip to another country.

es.L: Y comenzó a hablarles en parábolas: «Un hombre plantó una viña, y le puso una cerca alrededor, y cavó una pila bajo el lagar, y construyó una torre, y la arrendó a labradores, y se fue al extranjero.
es.B: Entonces comenzó a enseñarles en parábolas: «Un hombre plantó una viña y la rodeó con un cerco. Cavó una pila al pie del lagar y levantó una torre de vigilancia. Luego dejó la viña a cargo de unos arrendatarios y se fue a otro país.
es.R: Jesús comenzó a enseñarles con historias: «Había un hombre que plantó vides en un campo. Le puso una cerca alrededor. Cavó un pozo en la roca para recoger el jugo cuando se exprimían las uvas. Construyó una torre para que un guardia vigilara las vides. Luego alquiló la viña a unos labradores y se fue de viaje por mucho tiempo a otro país.

sw.L: Naye alianza kusema nao kwa mifano: "Mtu alipanda shamba la mizabibu, akaweka ua kulizunguka, akachimba shimo chini ya mahali pa kukamulia zabibu, akajenga mnara, akalikodisha kwa wakulima, akaenda ng'ambo.
sw.B: Kisha alianza kuwafundisha kwa mifano: "Palikuwa na mtu aliyepanda shamba la mizabibu, akaweka ua kulizunguka. Alichimba shimo chini ya mahali pa kukamulia zabibu, akajenga mnara wa ulinzi. Kisha akawakodishia wakulima shamba hilo, akaenda nchi nyingine.
sw.R: Yesu alianza kuwafundisha kwa hadithi: "Palikuwa na mtu aliyepanda mizabibu katika shamba. Aliweka ua kulizunguka. Alichonga shimo katika mwamba ili kukinga maji ya zabibu zilipokamuliwa. Alijenga mnara ambapo mlinzi angeweza kuilinda mizabibu. Kisha aliwakodishia wakulima fulani shamba hilo, akasafiri safari ndefu kwenda nchi nyingine.

decisions.choice: a vineyard planted, fenced, with a vat and a tower: the song of the vineyard in Isaiah 5:1-2
alternatives: an ordinary farming story with no background
decisions.reason: Isaiah sings of a man who planted a vineyard, cleared it, built a tower in it and cut out a wine vat. There the vineyard is Israel, the people God cared for (Isaiah 5:7). Jesus' hearers in the temple would know the song, and the parable builds on it.

decisions.choice: leased it to tenant farmers: they worked the land and paid the owner a share of the crop
alternatives: hired workers paid by the day
decisions.reason: An owner who lived far away often let his land to tenants. They kept part of the harvest and owed him the rest as rent, which he collected through his agents (12:2).

decisions.choice: a vat under the winepress: a pit cut below the press to catch the juice
decisions.reason: The word means the trough under the press. Grapes were trodden in a shallow press cut in rock, and the juice ran down into the vat below.

decisions.choice: parables: the plural, though one parable follows
alternatives: several parables told at this time
decisions.reason: Mark uses the plural for Jesus' way of speaking in pictures, as in 3:23 and 4:2. Only one parable is given here.

decisions.choice: word pictures; a pit in the rock to catch the juice; where a guard could watch over the vines
alternatives: parables; a wine vat; a tower
decisions.reason: Readable explains the parable word, as in 3:23, and says what the vat and the tower were for.

decisions.choice: parábolas (L, B); historias (R)
decisions.reason: The term used throughout Mark, recorded once in this file. The plural is kept though one parable follows (meaning decision m4); Readable says "historias", as the English Readable explains the word as "word pictures".

decisions.choice: labradores (L, R); arrendatarios (B)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of these tenant farmers: the Greek word is simply "farmers", whom the lease makes tenants (meaning decision m2). Balanced says "arrendatarios", as the English Balanced says "tenants"; so the Balanced verb is "dejó a cargo" rather than a second "arrendó".

decisions.choice: mifano (L, B); hadithi (R)
decisions.reason: The term used throughout Mark, recorded once in this file. "Mfano" is the Swahili word for a parable, a story that compares; "methali" is a proverb. The plural is kept though one parable follows (meaning decision m4); Readable says "hadithi" (stories), as the English Readable explains the word.

decisions.choice: shimo chini ya mahali pa kukamulia zabibu (L, B); shimo katika mwamba ili kukinga maji ya zabibu (R)
decisions.reason: The vat was a pit cut below the press to catch the juice (meaning decision m3). "Shinikizo" is a press and is not known to most readers; the phrase says what the pit was for.

source.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς τῷ καιρῷ δοῦλον, ἵνα παρὰ τῶν γεωργῶν λάβῃ ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος·

records.literal_gloss: And he sent to the farmers at the season a slave, that from the farmers he might receive from the fruits of the vineyard;

en.L: And at the season he sent a slave to the tenant farmers, so that he might receive from the tenant farmers [a share] of the fruit of the vineyard;
en.B: When harvest time came, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect from them his share of the vineyard's crop.
en.R: When it was time to pick the grapes, the owner sent a servant to the farmers. The servant was to bring back the owner's part of the harvest.

es.L: Y a su tiempo envió a los labradores un esclavo, para recibir de los labradores [su parte] del fruto de la viña;
es.B: Cuando llegó el tiempo de la cosecha, envió un siervo a los arrendatarios para cobrarles la parte de la cosecha de la viña que le correspondía.
es.R: Cuando llegó el tiempo de recoger las uvas, el dueño envió un siervo a los labradores. El siervo debía traerle al dueño su parte de la cosecha.

sw.L: Na kwa wakati wake alimtuma mtumwa kwa wakulima, ili apokee kutoka kwa wakulima [sehemu] ya matunda ya shamba la mizabibu;
sw.B: Wakati wa mavuno ulipofika, alimtuma mtumishi kwa wakulima ili apokee kutoka kwao sehemu yake ya mavuno ya shamba la mizabibu.
sw.R: Wakati wa kuchuma zabibu ulipofika, mwenye shamba alimtuma mtumishi kwa wakulima. Mtumishi huyo alipaswa kumletea mwenye shamba sehemu yake ya mavuno.

decisions.choice: a slave: a man owned by the master and sent to act in his name
decisions.reason: The word means a slave. A slave sent by his master carried the master's authority, so the way the tenants treat him is the way they treat the owner.

decisions.choice: the slaves stand for the prophets God sent to his people
decisions.reason: The Scriptures call the prophets God's slaves and say he sent them again and again to a people who would not listen (Jeremiah 7:25-26; 2 Chronicles 36:15-16).

decisions.choice: at the season: when the harvest was ready
decisions.reason: The word means the right or appointed time. For a vineyard it is the time of harvest, when the rent was due.

decisions.choice: his share (B); the owner's part (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says he would receive "from" the fruit, meaning a part of it. Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavo (L); siervo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, recorded once in this file: Literal keeps that the man was owned and sent to act in his master's name (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say "siervo", as the English says "servant". The same through verse 5.

decisions.choice: mtumwa (L); mtumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, recorded once in this file: Literal keeps that the man was owned and sent to act in his master's name (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say "mtumishi", as the English says "servant". The same through verse 5.

source.text: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἔδειραν καὶ ἀπέστειλαν κενόν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken him they beat [him] and sent [him] away empty.

en.L: And taking him, they beat [him] and sent [him] away empty.
en.B: But they seized him, beat him and sent him off with nothing.
en.R: But the farmers grabbed the servant and beat him. Then they sent him away without any of the grapes.

es.L: Y agarrándolo, [lo] golpearon y [lo] despidieron vacío.
es.B: Pero ellos lo agarraron, lo golpearon y lo despidieron con las manos vacías.
es.R: Pero los labradores agarraron al siervo y le dieron una paliza. Después lo echaron sin darle nada de las uvas.

sw.L: Na wakimkamata, walimpiga, wakamfukuza mikono mitupu.
sw.B: Lakini wao walimkamata, wakampiga, wakamfukuza mikono mitupu.
sw.R: Lakini wakulima walimkamata mtumishi huyo, wakampiga. Kisha wakamfukuza bila kumpa zabibu yoyote.

decisions.choice: beat: thrashed, gave a beating
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to skin, and was used for beating someone hard.

decisions.choice: empty: without the share he came for
decisions.reason: He went back to the owner empty-handed, with none of the rent.

decisions.choice: without any of the grapes
decisions.reason: Readable says what he did not bring back.

source.text: καὶ πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἄλλον δοῦλον· κἀκεῖνον ἐκεφαλίωσαν καὶ ἠτίμασαν.

records.literal_gloss: And again he sent to them another slave; and that one they struck on the head and dishonored.

en.L: And again he sent another slave to them; and that one they wounded in the head and treated shamefully.
en.B: He sent them another servant, and they struck this one on the head and insulted him.
en.R: The owner sent another servant to them. They hit this one on the head and treated him with shame.

es.L: Y de nuevo les envió otro esclavo; y a ese lo hirieron en la cabeza y [lo] deshonraron.
es.B: Les envió otro siervo, y a este lo golpearon en la cabeza y lo insultaron.
es.R: El dueño les envió otro siervo. A este le pegaron en la cabeza y lo trataron con desprecio.

sw.L: Na tena aliwatumia mtumwa mwingine; na huyo walimjeruhi kichwani na kumwaibisha.
sw.B: Akawatumia mtumishi mwingine, nao wakampiga kichwani na kumtukana.
sw.R: Mwenye shamba aliwatumia mtumishi mwingine. Walimpiga kichwani, wakamtendea mambo ya aibu.

decisions.choice: that one they struck on the head, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add that they threw stones at him before striking his head. The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: wounded in the head: struck on the head
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It comes from the word for head and most likely means a blow to the head. It can mean to sum up or to cut short, but that sense does not fit a beating.

decisions.choice: treated shamefully: insulted, disgraced
decisions.reason: The tenants add shame to violence. Each slave is treated worse than the last.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: καὶ ἄλλον ἀπέστειλεν· κἀκεῖνον ἀπέκτειναν, καὶ πολλοὺς ἄλλους, οὓς μὲν δέροντες οὓς δὲ ἀποκτέννοντες.

records.literal_gloss: And another he sent; and that one they killed, and many others, some beating, some killing.

en.L: And he sent another, and that one they killed; and many others, beating some and killing some.
en.B: He sent yet another, and him they killed. It went the same way with many others: some they beat, and some they killed.
en.R: The owner sent another servant, and they killed him. He sent many more servants. The farmers beat some of them and killed others.

es.L: Y envió a otro; y a ese lo mataron; y a muchos otros, golpeando a unos y matando a otros.
es.B: Envió todavía a otro, y a ese lo mataron. Lo mismo pasó con muchos otros: a unos los golpearon y a otros los mataron.
es.R: El dueño envió otro siervo, y lo mataron. Envió muchos siervos más. Los labradores golpearon a algunos y mataron a otros.

sw.L: Na alimtuma mwingine; na huyo walimuua; na wengine wengi, wengine wakiwapiga na wengine wakiwaua.
sw.B: Alimtuma mwingine tena, naye wakamuua. Ndivyo ilivyokuwa kwa wengine wengi: wengine waliwapiga, na wengine waliwaua.
sw.R: Mwenye shamba alimtuma mtumishi mwingine, nao wakamuua. Alituma watumishi wengi zaidi. Wakulima waliwapiga baadhi yao na kuwaua wengine.

decisions.choice: and many others: the verb is left out, they treated many others in the same way
alternatives: he sent many others, with no word on how they were treated
decisions.reason: The sentence breaks off and lets the reader supply the verb. The two "some ... some" phrases show what happened to them.

decisions.choice: they killed: the story of the prophets rejected and put to death
decisions.reason: Israel's history tells of prophets who were mocked and killed (1 Kings 19:10; 2 Chronicles 24:20-21). Mark has already told of John the Baptizer's death (6:17-29).

decisions.choice: It went the same way with many others (B); He sent many more servants (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply what the Greek leaves out.

source.text: ἔτι ἕνα εἶχεν, υἱὸν ἀγαπητόν· ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν ἔσχατον πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων ὅτι Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.

records.literal_gloss: Still one he had, a son beloved; he sent him last to them, saying that, They will respect the son of me.

en.L: He still had one, a beloved son; he sent him to them last, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
en.B: He had one left to send, his dearly loved son. Last of all he sent him to them, thinking, 'They will show respect for my son.'
en.R: The owner had one more person he could send. It was his own son, whom he loved very much. He sent him last of all. He thought, 'They will respect my son.'

es.L: Todavía tenía uno, un hijo amado; lo envió a ellos el último, diciendo: “Respetarán a mi hijo”.
es.B: Le quedaba todavía uno por enviar: su hijo amado. Por último se lo envió a ellos, pensando: “A mi hijo lo van a respetar”.
es.R: Al dueño le quedaba una persona más para enviar. Era su propio hijo, a quien amaba mucho. Lo envió el último de todos. Pensó: “A mi hijo sí lo respetarán”.

sw.L: Bado alikuwa na mmoja, mwana mpendwa; alimtuma kwao wa mwisho, akisema, 'Watamheshimu mwanangu.'
sw.B: Alikuwa amebaki na mmoja wa kumtuma, mwanawe mpendwa. Mwishowe alimtuma kwao, akifikiri, 'Mwanangu watamheshimu.'
sw.R: Mwenye shamba alikuwa na mtu mmoja zaidi wa kumtuma. Huyo alikuwa mwanawe mwenyewe, aliyempenda sana. Alimtuma mwisho kabisa. Alifikiri, 'Watamheshimu mwanangu.'

decisions.choice: a beloved son: the words God spoke of Jesus at his baptism and on the mountain
alternatives: only a detail of the story
decisions.reason: God called Jesus "my beloved Son" at his baptism (1:11) and on the mountain (9:7). Mark's readers hear in the parable Jesus' own story. The son is still a figure in the story; the parable leaves the hearers to see the point.

decisions.choice: respect: hold in honor, be ashamed to harm
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn toward someone with respect. The owner expects the tenants to treat his son as they would treat him.

decisions.choice: last: the final one sent; there is no one after him
decisions.reason: Sending the son is the owner's last step. After this, he will come himself (12:9).

decisions.choice: thinking
decisions.reason: The owner says this to himself. Balanced and Readable make that clear.

source.text: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οἱ γεωργοὶ πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς εἶπαν ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἡμῶν ἔσται ἡ κληρονομία.

records.literal_gloss: But those farmers to themselves said that, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and ours will be the inheritance.

en.L: But those tenant farmers said to one another, 'This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'
en.B: But the tenants talked it over among themselves: 'This is the heir. Come on, we will put him to death, and the vineyard will be ours to keep.'
en.R: But the farmers said to each other, 'This is the son who will own the vineyard one day. Let us kill him. Then the vineyard will belong to us!'

es.L: Pero aquellos labradores dijeron entre sí: “Este es el heredero; {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}, matémoslo, y la herencia será nuestra”.
es.B: Pero los arrendatarios lo hablaron entre ellos: “Este es el heredero. {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, matémoslo, y la viña será nuestra”.
es.R: Pero los labradores se dijeron unos a otros: “Este es el hijo que algún día será dueño de la viña. ¡Matémoslo! Así la viña será nuestra”.

sw.L: Lakini wakulima wale walisema wao kwa wao, 'Huyu ndiye mrithi; njooni, tumuue, na urithi utakuwa wetu.'
sw.B: Lakini wakulima hao walishauriana wao kwa wao, 'Huyu ndiye mrithi. Njooni tumuue, na shamba hili litakuwa letu.'
sw.R: Lakini wakulima waliambiana, 'Huyu ndiye mwana atakayekuwa mwenye shamba siku moja. Tumuue! Kisha shamba litakuwa letu!'

decisions.choice: the heir: the son who would receive the vineyard after his father
alternatives: a servant sent to collect rent
decisions.reason: The tenants may think that with the heir dead, the land would fall to those who held it. The story does not explain their thinking. It shows that they want to own what was only lent to them.

decisions.choice: come, let us kill him: the words of Joseph's brothers
decisions.reason: Joseph's brothers said the same when they saw the son their father loved coming toward them (Genesis 37:20).

decisions.choice: the inheritance: the property the heir would receive
decisions.reason: The word is the noun that goes with heir. Here it is the vineyard itself.

decisions.choice: the vineyard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the property.

source.text: καὶ λαβόντες ἀπέκτειναν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken they killed him, and cast out him outside the vineyard.

en.L: And taking [him], they killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
en.B: So they seized him, put him to death and threw his body out of the vineyard.
en.R: So they grabbed the son and killed him. They threw his body out of the vineyard.

es.L: Y tomándolo, lo mataron y lo arrojaron fuera de la viña.
es.B: Así que lo agarraron, lo mataron y arrojaron su cuerpo fuera de la viña.
es.R: Entonces agarraron al hijo y lo mataron. Tiraron su cuerpo fuera de la viña.

sw.L: Na wakimkamata, walimuua, wakamtupa nje ya shamba la mizabibu.
sw.B: Basi walimkamata, wakamuua, wakautupa mwili wake nje ya shamba la mizabibu.
sw.R: Basi walimkamata mwana huyo, wakamuua. Waliutupa mwili wake nje ya shamba.

decisions.choice: threw him out: left his body unburied
decisions.reason: In Mark the son is killed first and then thrown out. To leave a body unburied was a great shame.

decisions.choice: killed, then threw out: the order of Mark's account
alternatives: threw him out, then killed him
decisions.reason: Matthew 21:39 and Luke 20:15 tell it the other way round, with the son taken out of the vineyard and then killed. Mark puts the killing first.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that he was already dead.

source.text: τί ποιήσει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος;

records.literal_gloss: What will do the master of the vineyard?

en.L: What will the master of the vineyard do?
en.B: So what will the owner of the vineyard do?
en.R: So what will the owner of the vineyard do?

es.L: ¿Qué hará el señor de la viña?
es.B: Entonces, ¿qué hará el dueño de la viña?
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué hará el dueño de la viña?

sw.L: Bwana wa shamba la mizabibu atafanya nini?
sw.B: Basi, mwenye shamba la mizabibu atafanya nini?
sw.R: Basi, mwenye shamba atafanya nini?

decisions.choice: master: the owner of the vineyard
decisions.reason: The word can mean owner or master, and it is also the word for Lord. In the story it is the owner, who stands for God.

decisions.choice: a question to the hearers
alternatives: a question to the disciples only
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 5:3-4, the hearers are asked to judge. Jesus gives the answer himself.

decisions.choice: owner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plainer word for the man who owns the vineyard.

source.text: ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργούς, καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις.

records.literal_gloss: He will come and will destroy the farmers and will give the vineyard to others.

en.L: He will come and destroy the tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.
en.B: He will come and put those tenants to death, and he will hand the vineyard over to others.
en.R: He will come and kill those farmers. Then he will give the vineyard to other people to take care of.

es.L: Vendrá y destruirá a los labradores, y dará la viña a otros.
es.B: Vendrá, dará muerte a esos arrendatarios y entregará la viña a otros.
es.R: Vendrá y matará a esos labradores. Luego les dará la viña a otras personas para que la cuiden.

sw.L: Atakuja na kuwaangamiza wakulima, na kuwapa wengine shamba la mizabibu.
sw.B: Atakuja, awaue wakulima hao, na kuwakabidhi wengine shamba la mizabibu.
sw.R: Atakuja na kuwaua wakulima hao. Kisha atawapa watu wengine shamba hilo walitunze.

decisions.choice: others: new keepers of the vineyard
decisions.reason: The vineyard is not destroyed; the tenants are. In Isaiah 5 God judges the vineyard itself. Here judgment falls on those in charge of it, and the leaders understand that the story is about them (12:12).

decisions.choice: destroy: put to death
decisions.reason: The verb means to destroy or kill.

decisions.choice: to take care of
decisions.reason: Readable says what the others will do with the vineyard.

source.text: οὐδὲ τὴν γραφὴν ταύτην ἀνέγνωτε· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας·

records.literal_gloss: Not even this Scripture have you read: [The] stone which rejected those building, this has become for head of [the] corner;

en.L: Have you not even read this Scripture: 'The stone that those building rejected, this has become the head of the corner;
en.B: Have you not even read this passage of Scripture: 'The stone that the builders threw away as useless has become the chief cornerstone.
en.R: Have you not read what the Scriptures say? 'The builders did not want a certain stone. But it has become the most important stone in the building.

es.L: ¿Ni siquiera {{plural_you:han|habéis}} leído esta Escritura: “La piedra que rechazaron los que construían, esta ha llegado a ser cabeza de [la] esquina;
es.B: ¿No {{plural_you:han|habéis}} leído siquiera este pasaje de las Escrituras: “La piedra que los constructores tiraron por inservible se ha convertido en la piedra angular principal.
es.R: ¿No {{plural_you:han|habéis}} leído lo que dicen las Escrituras? “Los constructores no quisieron cierta piedra. Pero esa piedra ha llegado a ser la más importante del edificio.

sw.L: Je, hamjasoma hata andiko hili: 'Jiwe ambalo wajenzi walilikataa, hilo limekuwa kichwa cha pembe;
sw.B: Je, hamjasoma hata sehemu hii ya Maandiko: 'Jiwe ambalo wajenzi walilitupa kuwa halifai limekuwa jiwe la msingi la pembeni.
sw.R: Je, hamjasoma yale ambayo Maandiko yanasema? 'Wajenzi hawakulitaka jiwe fulani. Lakini jiwe hilo limekuwa jiwe muhimu kuliko yote katika jengo.

decisions.choice: the stone the builders rejected: Psalm 118:22
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes Psalm 118:22-23, the psalm the crowd sang as he came into Jerusalem (11:9-10). In the psalm the stone stands for one whom people despised but God honored.

decisions.choice: the head of the corner: the stone that holds the corner of the building together
alternatives: the top stone of an arch or a gate
decisions.reason: The phrase means the main stone at the corner, where two walls meet and are bound together. Some take it as the stone set on top to finish the building. Either way it is the most important stone.

decisions.choice: the rejected stone is the son who is killed
alternatives: a separate saying about the temple
decisions.reason: The parable ends with the son killed; the psalm adds that the one rejected is set in the place of highest honor. Jesus has already said he will be rejected by the elders, chief priests and scribes and rise again (8:31).

decisions.choice: a separate question, then the quotation
alternatives: one question that holds the quotation
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question into two short sentences.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" (han|habéis)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the chapter.

source.text: παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;

en.L: this came about from [the] Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"

es.R: El Señor hizo esto, y nos llena de asombro”».

sw.B: Bwana ndiye aliyefanya jambo hili, nasi tunalitazama kwa mshangao'?"
sw.R: Bwana amefanya jambo hili, nalo linatushangaza.'"

decisions.choice: from the Lord: Psalm 118:23; the Hebrew has the divine name
decisions.reason: Where the Greek has "Lord", the Hebrew psalm has the divine name. It is God himself who raised the rejected stone to honor.

decisions.choice: this: the turn of events, the rejected stone made the cornerstone
decisions.reason: The word is feminine, as in the Greek translation of the psalm, and most likely refers to the whole event.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: The New Testament quotes the psalm in Greek with the word for Lord, so every level writes Lord, as at 11:9. The meaning note gives the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: a statement, with no question mark
decisions.reason: Readable turned the question of 12:10 into a statement, so the quotation ends without one.

source.text: Καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν ὄχλον, ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν εἶπεν.

records.literal_gloss: And they were seeking him to seize, and they feared the crowd; for they knew that against them the parable he spoke.

en.L: And they were seeking to seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and [yet] they feared the crowd; for they knew that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken the parable against them.
en.B: The leaders wanted to arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but they were afraid of the crowd. They knew that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had aimed the parable at them.
en.R: The leaders understood that Jesus had told this story against them. So they wanted to arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But they were afraid of the crowd.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} buscaban apresar, y [sin embargo] temieron a la multitud; porque sabían que había dicho la parábola contra ellos.
es.B: Los dirigentes {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} querían arrestar, pero tenían miedo de la multitud. Sabían que había dirigido la parábola contra ellos.
es.R: Los dirigentes entendieron que Jesús había contado esa historia contra ellos. Por eso {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} querían arrestar. Pero tenían miedo de la gente.

sw.L: Na walikuwa wakitafuta kumkamata, na [hata hivyo] waliuogopa umati; kwa maana walijua kwamba ameusema mfano ule dhidi yao.
sw.B: Viongozi walitaka kumkamata, lakini waliuogopa umati wa watu. Walijua kwamba mfano ule aliusema kwa kuwalenga wao.
sw.R: Viongozi walielewa kwamba Yesu alikuwa amesimulia hadithi hiyo dhidi yao. Kwa hiyo walitaka kumkamata. Lakini waliuogopa umati wa watu.

decisions.choice: they: the chief priests, scribes and elders of 11:27
decisions.reason: The subject is the group that questioned Jesus' authority (11:27-33). They are still listening.

decisions.choice: and: here with the force of "but"
decisions.reason: They wanted to arrest him and yet did not dare. The plain "and" joins two things that pull against each other.

decisions.choice: against them: aimed at them, about them
decisions.reason: They see that they are the tenants in the story.

decisions.choice: The leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who was seeking to arrest him. Readable puts the reason first.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns, pronouns before the verb and possessives (lo)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("había dicho") and can join an object pronoun to the end of the verb ("arrestarlo"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. Here "lo" goes before the verb so it can carry the setting. So the setting covers fewer words than in English; this holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on kumkamata (to seize him) or ameusema (he had spoken)
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb, and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("yake", "yeye", "wangu"). Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθον.

records.literal_gloss: And having left him they went away.

en.L: And leaving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they went away.
en.B: So they left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and went off.
en.R: So they left Jesus and went away.

es.L: Y dejándolo, se fueron.
es.B: Así que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dejaron y se marcharon.
es.R: Así que dejaron a Jesús y se fueron.

sw.L: Na wakimwacha, waliondoka.
sw.B: Basi wakamwacha, wakaenda zao.
sw.R: Basi walimwacha Yesu, wakaondoka.

decisions.choice: they left him: for now they give up the attempt
alternatives: they left the temple for good
decisions.reason: They go away, but the questions that follow show they have not stopped trying to trap him (12:13).

source.text: Καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν πρὸς αὐτόν τινας τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ἵνα αὐτὸν ἀγρεύσωσιν λόγῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And they send to him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that him they might catch in a word.

en.L: And they send to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, so that they might catch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in [something {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would] say.
en.B: Then they sent some Pharisees and Herodians to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own words.
en.R: Then the leaders sent some Pharisees to Jesus. They also sent some people who supported King Herod. They wanted to catch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saying something wrong.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} envían algunos de los fariseos y de los herodianos, para que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} atrapen en [alguna] palabra.
es.B: Luego {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} enviaron a algunos fariseos y herodianos para que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hicieran caer con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} propias palabras.
es.R: Luego los dirigentes enviaron a algunos fariseos a ver a Jesús. También enviaron a unos hombres que apoyaban al rey Herodes. Querían {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sorprender diciendo algo indebido.

sw.L: Na wanatuma {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} baadhi ya Mafarisayo na wafuasi wa Herode, ili wamnase kwa neno.
sw.B: Kisha walimtumia baadhi ya Mafarisayo na wafuasi wa Herode ili wamnase kwa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe.
sw.R: Kisha viongozi waliwatuma baadhi ya Mafarisayo kwa Yesu. Waliwatuma pia watu fulani waliomuunga mkono Mfalme Herode. Walitaka kumnasa akisema jambo baya.

decisions.choice: they send: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense. The sense is past. The senders are the leaders of 11:27 and 12:12.

decisions.choice: Pharisees and Herodians: strict teachers of the law and supporters of Herod's family
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were a movement that kept the law and its traditions with care. The Herodians backed Herod Antipas, the ruler of Galilee under Rome. The two had already plotted together against Jesus (3:6).

decisions.choice: catch: hunt, trap as an animal is trapped
decisions.reason: The verb is used for catching game. They hope his own words will snare him.

decisions.choice: people who supported King Herod
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Herodians were, as at 3:6.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (envían); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (enviaron)
decisions.reason: Mark tells parts of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verses 14, 16 and 18.

decisions.choice: los herodianos (L, B); unos hombres que apoyaban al rey Herodes (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, recorded once in this file: "herodianos" is the established Spanish name for the party (meaning decision m2); Readable says who they were, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanatuma); past at Balanced and Readable (walimtumia)
decisions.reason: Mark tells parts of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same in verses 14, 16 and 18.

decisions.choice: wafuasi wa Herode (supporters of Herod)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of the Herodians (meaning decision m2), recorded once in this file. Swahili has no established word for the party, and "Maherodi" would read as several men named Herod.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθόντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλ’ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκεις· ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ;

records.literal_gloss: And having come they say to him, Teacher, we know that true you are and not there is care to you about no one; for not you look at [the] face of men, but on [the basis of] truth the way of God you teach. Is it lawful to give tax to Caesar or not?

en.L: And coming, they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are true and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not care about anyone, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not look at the face of {{gender:people|men}}, but teach the way of God on the basis of truth. Is it lawful to pay the poll tax to Caesar or not?
en.B: They came and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we are sure that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a man of integrity and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are not swayed by anyone. You pay no attention to a person's rank, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach the way of God in truth. Is it right to pay the tax to Caesar, or not?
en.R: They came to Jesus and said, "Teacher, we are sure that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are honest. You do not worry about what anyone thinks of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. It does not matter to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} how important people are. You teach the truth about the way God wants people to live. So tell us, does God's law allow us to pay taxes to Caesar, the Roman emperor, or not?

es.L: Y viniendo, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen: «Maestro, sabemos que eres veraz y que no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} importa nadie, porque no miras [el] rostro de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}, sino que con verdad enseñas el camino de Dios. ¿Es lícito dar el tributo personal al César, o no?
es.B: Llegaron y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Maestro, sabemos que eres un hombre íntegro y que no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dejas influir por nadie. No juzgas a nadie por su posición, sino que enseñas el camino de Dios de acuerdo con la verdad. ¿Está permitido pagar el tributo al César, o no?
es.R: Fueron a ver a Jesús. «Maestro», dijeron, «sabemos que eres honesto. No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} preocupa lo que la gente piense de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} importa si una persona es importante o no. Enseñas la verdad sobre la manera en que Dios quiere que la gente viva. Entonces dinos: ¿permite la ley de Dios que paguemos impuestos al César, el emperador romano, o no?

sw.L: Na wakija, wanamwambia, "Mwalimu, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mkweli, wala humjali mtu yeyote, kwa maana hutazami uso wa watu, bali kwa kweli unafundisha njia ya Mungu. Je, ni halali kulipa kodi ya kichwa kwa Kaisari, au la?
sw.B: Walifika, wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, tuna hakika kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mtu mnyoofu, na kwamba hakuna mtu anayekuyumbisha. Huangalii cheo cha mtu, bali unafundisha njia ya Mungu kwa kweli. Je, ni sawa kulipa kodi kwa Kaisari, au la?
sw.R: Walikuja kwa Yesu, wakasema, "Mwalimu, tuna hakika kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwaminifu. Huhangaiki na mawazo ya watu kukuhusu. Haijalishi kwako kama mtu ni mkubwa au la. Unafundisha ukweli kuhusu njia ambayo Mungu anataka watu waishi. Basi tuambie, je, sheria ya Mungu inaturuhusu kulipa kodi kwa Kaisari, mtawala mkuu wa Roma, au la?

decisions.choice: look at the face of people: judge by a person's rank or appearance
decisions.reason: To look at someone's face meant to favor them because of who they were. They say Jesus shows no such favor.

decisions.choice: the tax to Caesar: the yearly tax each person in Judea paid to Rome
decisions.reason: The word is the Latin word for a census. Judea had been under direct Roman rule since AD 6, and the tax was resented as a sign of foreign rule. A revolt had been raised against it in that year (Acts 5:37).

decisions.choice: flattering words that set a trap
decisions.reason: If Jesus says yes, he loses the people who hate the tax. If he says no, he can be reported to Rome as a rebel (12:13, 15).

decisions.choice: true: honest, a man who speaks the truth
decisions.reason: They mean that he says what is true whatever the cost.

decisions.choice: the way God wants people to live; does God's law allow us; the Roman emperor
alternatives: the way of God; is it lawful; Caesar
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the way of God" and "lawful" refer to, and who Caesar was.

decisions.choice: tributo personal (L); tributo (B); impuestos (R)
decisions.reason: The tax was the yearly tax each person in Judea paid to Rome (meaning decision m2). "Censo" is the Latin loanword but today means a census; Literal says "personal" to show that the tax fell on each person.

decisions.choice: kodi ya kichwa (L); kodi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The tax was the yearly tax each person in Judea paid to Rome (meaning decision m2). "Kodi ya kichwa" is the Swahili name for a poll tax; "ushuru" is a duty on goods.

source.text: δῶμεν ἢ μὴ δῶμεν;

records.literal_gloss: Should we give, or not should we give?

en.L: Should we pay, or should we not pay?"
en.B: Are we to pay or not?"
en.R: Should we pay them or not?"

es.L: ¿Debemos pagar o no debemos pagar?».
es.B: ¿Lo pagamos o no?».
es.R: ¿Debemos pagarlos o no?».

sw.L: Tulipe, au tusilipe?"
sw.B: Je, tulipe au tusilipe?"
sw.R: Je, tuilipe kodi hiyo au tusiilipe?"

decisions.choice: should we pay: a question that asks for a plain yes or no
decisions.reason: They press for a short answer that will commit him either way.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὴν ὑπόκρισιν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί με πειράζετε;

records.literal_gloss: But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, Why me do you test?

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, "Why are you testing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw through their pretense and said to them, "Why are you trying to trap {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: But Jesus knew they were only pretending. He said to them, "Why are you trying to trick {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, conociendo su hipocresía, les dijo: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} a prueba?
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se dio cuenta de su fingimiento y les dijo: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:tienden|tendéis}} una trampa?
es.R: Pero Jesús sabía que solo estaban fingiendo. Les dijo: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} engañar?

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, akijua unafiki wao, aliwaambia, "Kwa nini mnanijaribu?
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliutambua unafiki wao, akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnajaribu kuninasa?
sw.R: Lakini Yesu alijua kwamba walikuwa wakijifanya tu. Akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnajaribu kunidanganya?

decisions.choice: hypocrisy: playing a part, saying what one does not mean
decisions.reason: The word was used for an actor on a stage. Their praise was a mask for their plan.

decisions.choice: test: put to the test in order to trap
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when the Pharisees test Jesus in 8:11 and 10:2.

decisions.choice: pretense, trying to trap (B); only pretending, trying to trick (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for what they were doing.

source.text: φέρετέ μοι δηνάριον ἵνα ἴδω.

records.literal_gloss: Bring me a denarius that I might see.

en.L: Bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a denarius so that I may look [at it]."
en.B: Bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{units:a silver coin worth a day's wage|a denarius}} so I can look at it."
en.R: Bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{units:a silver coin, the kind a worker earns in a day|a denarius}}. Let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} look at it."

es.L: {{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} un denario para que [lo] vea».
es.B: {{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} {{units:una moneda de plata que vale el salario de un día|un denario}} para echarle un vistazo».
es.R: {{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} {{units:una moneda de plata, de las que gana un trabajador en un día|un denario}}. {{plural_you:Déjenme|Dejadme}} echarle un vistazo».

sw.L: Nileteeni dinari niione."
sw.B: Nileteeni {{units:sarafu ya fedha yenye thamani ya mshahara wa siku moja|dinari}} niiangalie."
sw.R: Nileteeni {{units:sarafu ya fedha, kiasi ambacho mfanyakazi hulipwa kwa siku moja|dinari}}. Nataka kuiangalia."

decisions.choice: a denarius: a Roman silver coin, a day's pay for a laborer
decisions.reason: The denarius was the coin in which the tax was paid. It bore the emperor's head and a title (12:16). A denarius was a day's wage for a farm worker (Matthew 20:2).

decisions.choice: bring me: Jesus has them produce the coin
alternatives: Jesus takes a coin from his own purse
decisions.reason: He does not take out a coin himself. They have to bring one, and so show that they use Caesar's money.

decisions.choice: a silver coin worth a day's wage (B); a silver coin, the kind a worker earns in a day (R); a denarius as the original unit
decisions.reason: The units setting gives the value of the coin by default and its name as the alternative, as at 6:37. Literal keeps the coin.

decisions.choice: {{units:una moneda de plata que vale el salario de un día|un denario}}
decisions.reason: As in English and in Matthew 22:19: Balanced and Readable say what the coin was worth, a day's pay (meaning decision m1), with the coin's name as the alternative. Literal keeps the coin. "Echarle un vistazo" fits both wordings, "moneda" and "denario".

decisions.choice: {{units:sarafu ya fedha yenye thamani ya mshahara wa siku moja|dinari}}
decisions.reason: As in English and in Matthew 22:19: Balanced and Readable say what the coin was worth, a day's pay (meaning decision m1), with "dinari" as the alternative. Literal keeps the coin.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν.

records.literal_gloss: And they brought.

en.L: And they brought [one].
en.B: They brought one.
en.R: So they brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a coin.

es.L: Y ellos trajeron [uno].
es.B: Ellos trajeron la moneda.
es.R: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trajeron una moneda.

sw.L: Nao wakaleta [moja].
sw.B: Wakaileta.
sw.R: Basi wakamletea sarafu.

decisions.choice: they brought: one of them had a coin at hand
alternatives: they went away to fetch one
decisions.reason: Mark's short sentence suggests they had one ready, even in the temple courts.

decisions.choice: him a coin
decisions.reason: Readable says what they brought and to whom.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Whose [is] the image this and the inscription?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Whose image [is] this, and [whose] inscription?"
en.B: He asked them, "Whose face is this, and whose name is written here?"
en.R: Jesus asked them, "Whose picture is on this coin? And whose name is written on it?"

es.L: Y les dice: «¿De quién [es] esta imagen, y [de quién] la inscripción?».
es.B: Les preguntó: «¿De quién es este rostro, y de quién es el nombre que está escrito aquí?».
es.R: Jesús les preguntó: «¿De quién es la cara que está en esta moneda? ¿Y de quién es el nombre que tiene escrito?».

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Ya nani sura hii, na maandishi [haya]?"
sw.B: Akawauliza, "Uso huu ni wa nani, na jina lililoandikwa hapa ni la nani?"
sw.R: Yesu akawauliza, "Picha iliyo kwenye sarafu hii ni ya nani? Na jina lililoandikwa juu yake ni la nani?"

decisions.choice: he says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: image: a likeness, here the head stamped on the coin
decisions.reason: The word means an image or likeness. The coin of that time showed the emperor's head, with words naming him.

decisions.choice: image: a possible echo of the image of God
decisions.reason: The same word is used in the Greek of Genesis 1:26-27, where people are made in God's image. If the echo is meant, what bears God's image belongs to God (12:17). Mark does not say so.

decisions.choice: face, name written (B); picture, name written (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the image and the inscription were.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος.

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Caesar's.

en.L: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Caesar's."
en.B: "Caesar's," they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They answered, "Caesar's. It is the emperor's."

es.L: Y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Del César».
es.B: «Del César», {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron.
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «Del César. Es del emperador».

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia, "Ya Kaisari."
sw.B: "Ya Kaisari," wakamjibu.
sw.R: Wakajibu, "Ya Kaisari. Ni ya mtawala mkuu wa Roma."

decisions.choice: Caesar: the title of the Roman emperor, at this time Tiberius
decisions.reason: Caesar was the family name of Julius Caesar and became the title of the emperors. Tiberius ruled from AD 14 to 37.

decisions.choice: It is the emperor's
decisions.reason: Readable says who Caesar was.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τὰ Καίσαρος ἀπόδοτε Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to them, The things of Caesar give back to Caesar and the things of God to God.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "Give back to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Pay back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God."
en.R: Jesus told them, "Give Caesar what belongs to him. And give God what belongs to God."

es.L: Y Jesús les dijo: «Lo del César {{plural_you:devuélvanlo|devolvedlo}} al César, y lo de Dios, a Dios».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Devuelvan|Devolved}} al César lo que le pertenece al César, y a Dios lo que le pertenece a Dios».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Denle|Dadle}} al César lo que es suyo. Y {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} a Dios lo que es de Dios».

sw.L: Naye Yesu akawaambia, "Vya Kaisari mrudishieni Kaisari, na vya Mungu [mrudishieni] Mungu."
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Mrudishieni Kaisari kilicho mali ya Kaisari, na Mungu kilicho mali ya Mungu."
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Mpeni Kaisari kilicho chake. Na mpeni Mungu kilicho cha Mungu."

decisions.choice: give back: pay what is owed
decisions.reason: They asked whether they should "give". Jesus uses a verb that means to give back or repay, as one pays a debt.

decisions.choice: the things of God: what belongs to God, a claim greater than Caesar's
decisions.reason: The coin bears Caesar's image and goes back to him. People belong to God, and God's claim covers the whole of life. Jesus answers the trap without siding with the rebels or simply with Rome.

decisions.choice: two short commands
decisions.reason: Readable gives each command on its own.

decisions.choice: devolver (L, B); dar (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "give back", pay what is owed (meaning decision m1), not the "give" of their question in verse 14. Literal and Balanced say "devolver"; Readable says "dar", as the English Readable says "give".

decisions.choice: kurudishia (L, B); kupa (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "give back", pay what is owed (meaning decision m1), not the "give" of their question in verse 14. Literal and Balanced say "mrudishieni"; Readable says "mpeni", as the English Readable says "give".

en.R: They were amazed at Jesus' answer.

es.B: Quedaron asombrados de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

decisions.choice: Jesus' answer
decisions.reason: Readable says what amazed them.

decisions.choice: Sadducees: a party of leading priests and wealthy families
decisions.reason: The Sadducees held power in the temple. They denied that the dead will rise (Acts 23:8). This is their only appearance in Mark.

decisions.choice: resurrection: the dead raised to life at the end
alternatives: the soul living on after death
decisions.reason: The word means a rising up. The hope was that God would raise the dead bodily at the last day (Daniel 12:2).

decisions.choice: come: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: a group of Jewish leaders who said that people who die will not come back to life
alternatives: who say there is no resurrection
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Sadducees were and what resurrection means.

source.text: Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ὅτι ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ καὶ καταλίπῃ γυναῖκα καὶ μὴ ἀφῇ τέκνον, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if of anyone a brother should die and leave behind a wife and not leave a child, that should take the brother of him the wife and raise up seed for the brother of him.

en.L: "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone's brother dies and leaves behind a wife and does not leave a child, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
en.B: "Teacher, Moses gave us this rule in writing: if a man dies and leaves a wife but no child, his brother is to marry the widow and father children to carry on the dead man's family.
en.R: "Teacher, Moses wrote a law for us. It says that if a man dies and has no children, his brother must marry the widow. Then their children will be counted as the dead brother's children.

es.L: «Maestro, Moisés nos escribió que si el hermano de alguien muere y deja mujer y no deja hijo, que su hermano tome la mujer y levante descendencia a su hermano.
es.B: «Maestro, Moisés nos dejó por escrito esta norma: si un hombre muere y deja esposa pero ningún hijo, su hermano debe casarse con la viuda y darle hijos que continúen la familia del difunto.
es.R: «Maestro, Moisés escribió una ley para nosotros. Dice que si un hombre muere sin tener hijos, su hermano tiene que casarse con la viuda. Así, los hijos que tengan contarán como hijos del hermano que murió.

sw.L: "Mwalimu, Musa alituandikia kwamba ndugu wa mtu akifa na kuacha mke na asiache mtoto, ndugu yake amchukue mke huyo na kumwinulia ndugu yake uzao.
sw.B: "Mwalimu, Musa alituandikia agizo hili: mtu akifa na kuacha mke bila mtoto, ndugu yake anapaswa kumwoa mjane huyo na kumzalia ndugu yake watoto ili jamaa ya marehemu iendelee.
sw.R: "Mwalimu, Musa alituandikia sheria. Inasema kwamba mtu akifa bila kuwa na watoto, ndugu yake lazima amwoe mjane. Kisha watoto watakaozaliwa watahesabiwa kuwa watoto wa ndugu aliyekufa.

decisions.choice: Moses wrote: the law of Deuteronomy 25:5-6
decisions.reason: The law says that when a man dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow, and her first son will carry on the dead man's name. Genesis 38:8 shows the same custom.

decisions.choice: raise up offspring for his brother: so that the dead man's name and land stay in his family
decisions.reason: The child would be counted as the dead man's heir. The custom kept a family's name and land from being lost in Israel.

decisions.choice: seed: offspring, children
decisions.reason: Seed is a common way of speaking of descendants.

decisions.choice: a man (B, R); children to carry on the dead man's family (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the case more simply and say what raising up offspring meant.

source.text: ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα, καὶ ἀποθνῄσκων οὐκ ἀφῆκεν σπέρμα·

records.literal_gloss: Seven brothers there were; and the first took a wife, and dying not left seed;

en.L: There were seven brothers; and the first took a wife, and dying, he left no offspring;
en.B: Once there were seven brothers. The first of them married, and he died without leaving any children.
en.R: There were seven brothers. The oldest brother got married, but he died without having any children.

es.L: Había siete hermanos; y el primero tomó mujer, y al morir no dejó descendencia;
es.B: Pues bien, había una vez siete hermanos. El primero se casó y murió sin dejar hijos.
es.R: Había siete hermanos. El hermano mayor se casó, pero murió sin tener hijos.

sw.L: Palikuwa na ndugu saba; na wa kwanza alioa mke, na alipokufa hakuacha uzao;
sw.B: Palikuwa na ndugu saba. Wa kwanza alioa, akafariki bila kuacha watoto.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na ndugu saba. Ndugu mkubwa kuliko wote alioa, lakini akafa bila kupata watoto.

decisions.choice: there were seven brothers: a made-up case
decisions.reason: The Sadducees tell a story meant to make the resurrection look absurd.

decisions.choice: took a wife: married
alternatives: took a wife as a slave
decisions.reason: This is the usual way of saying a man married.

decisions.choice: the oldest brother
decisions.reason: Readable says who "the first" was.

source.text: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν, καὶ ἀπέθανεν μὴ καταλιπὼν σπέρμα, καὶ ὁ τρίτος ὡσαύτως·

records.literal_gloss: And the second took her and died not having left behind seed; and the third likewise;

en.L: And the second took her and died, leaving behind no offspring; and the third likewise;
en.B: The second brother married her and died, again leaving no children, and the third did the same.
en.R: Then the second brother married the widow, but he also died without children. The same thing happened with the third brother.

es.L: Y el segundo la tomó, y murió sin dejar descendencia; y el tercero igualmente;
es.B: El segundo se casó con ella y murió, también sin dejar hijos, y con el tercero pasó lo mismo.
es.R: Luego el segundo hermano se casó con la viuda, pero también murió sin hijos. Lo mismo le pasó al tercer hermano.

sw.L: Na wa pili alimchukua, akafa bila kuacha uzao; na wa tatu vivyo hivyo;
sw.B: Ndugu wa pili alimwoa, naye pia akafa bila kuacha watoto, na wa tatu vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Kisha ndugu wa pili alimwoa mjane huyo, lakini naye pia akafa bila watoto. Jambo hilo hilo lilimtokea ndugu wa tatu.

decisions.choice: each brother keeps the law in turn
decisions.reason: Each brother does what the law of 12:19 requires, and each dies childless.

decisions.choice: again (B); also (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the second death repeats the first.

source.text: καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐκ ἀφῆκαν σπέρμα· ἔσχατον πάντων καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν.

en.B: None of the seven left any children. Last of all, the woman died too.
en.R: All seven brothers married her, and none of them had children. Finally the woman died too.

es.L: Y los siete no dejaron descendencia. Al final de todos, murió también la mujer.
es.B: Ninguno de los siete dejó hijos. Por último, murió también la mujer.
es.R: Los siete hermanos se casaron con ella, y ninguno tuvo hijos. Al final, también murió la mujer.

sw.L: Na wale saba hawakuacha uzao. Mwisho wa wote yule mwanamke naye alikufa.
sw.B: Hakuna hata mmoja kati ya wale saba aliyeacha watoto. Mwisho wa wote, yule mwanamke naye akafariki.
sw.R: Ndugu wote saba walimwoa, na hakuna aliyepata watoto. Mwishowe yule mwanamke naye akafa.

decisions.choice: and the seven left no offspring, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: and the seven took her and left no offspring
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add that all seven took her. The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: last of all: after all the brothers
decisions.reason: The story ends with the whole family dead.

decisions.choice: All seven brothers married her
decisions.reason: Readable restates what the seven had done.

source.text: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν τίνος αὐτῶν ἔσται γυνή;

en.L: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife of them will she be?
en.B: At the resurrection, when they rise again, which of them will she be married to?
en.R: So when the dead come back to life, whose wife will she be?

es.L: En la resurrección, cuando resuciten, ¿de cuál de ellos será esposa?
es.B: En la resurrección, cuando vuelvan a la vida, ¿con cuál de ellos estará casada?
es.R: Entonces, cuando los muertos vuelvan a la vida, ¿de quién será esposa?

sw.L: Katika ufufuo, watakapofufuka, atakuwa mke wa yupi kati yao?
sw.B: Siku ya ufufuo, watakapofufuka, atakuwa mke wa yupi kati yao?
sw.R: Basi wafu watakaporudi kuwa hai, mwanamke huyu atakuwa mke wa nani?

decisions.choice: when they rise, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some important manuscripts leave out these words, which repeat the sense of "in the resurrection". The SBLGNT keeps them. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: whose wife: a question meant to mock
decisions.reason: The Sadducees assume that if there were a resurrection, life would go on just as now, and so the law of Moses would end in a tangle.

decisions.choice: when the dead come back to life
alternatives: in the resurrection, when they rise
decisions.reason: Readable says what resurrection is in plain words.

source.text: οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.

records.literal_gloss: For the seven had her as wife.

en.L: For the seven had her as wife."
en.B: All seven had her as their wife."
en.R: All seven brothers were married to her!"

es.L: Porque los siete la tuvieron por esposa».
es.B: Los siete la tuvieron como esposa».
es.R: ¡Los siete hermanos estuvieron casados con ella!».

sw.L: Kwa maana wale saba walikuwa naye kama mke."
sw.B: Wote saba walimwoa."
sw.R: Ndugu wote saba walikuwa wamemwoa!"

decisions.choice: for: the reason the question seems to have no answer
decisions.reason: Each brother had an equal claim.

source.text: ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐ διὰ τοῦτο πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: Said to them Jesus, Not because of this do you err, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God?

en.L: Jesus said to them, "Is this not why you are going astray, that you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Is not this the reason you are mistaken: you know neither the Scriptures nor God's power?
en.R: Jesus answered, "You are wrong, because you do not know what the Scriptures say. And you do not know God's power.

es.L: Jesús les dijo: «¿No es por esto que {{plural_you:andan|andáis}} extraviados, porque no {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} las Escrituras ni el poder de Dios?
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «¿No es esta la razón de que {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} equivocados: que no {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} ni las Escrituras ni el poder de Dios?
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} equivocados, porque no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que dicen las Escrituras. Y no {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} el poder de Dios.

sw.L: Yesu aliwaambia, "Je, si kwa sababu hii mnapotea, kwa kuwa hamyajui Maandiko wala nguvu ya Mungu?
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Je, sababu ya kukosea kwenu si hii: kwamba hamyajui Maandiko wala uweza wa Mungu?
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Mmekosea, kwa sababu hamjui Maandiko yanasema nini. Tena hamjui nguvu ya Mungu.

decisions.choice: is this not why: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question form makes a firm charge: this is the cause of their error.

decisions.choice: going astray: wandering from the truth, being mistaken
decisions.reason: The verb means to wander off the road. Jesus uses it again in 12:27.

decisions.choice: two failures: not knowing the Scriptures, and not knowing God's power
decisions.reason: They do not see what the Scriptures say about the dead (12:26), and they do not believe God can make a new life unlike this one (12:25).

decisions.choice: statements
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects.

source.text: ὅταν γὰρ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῶσιν, οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται, ἀλλ’ εἰσὶν ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: When for out from [the] dead they rise, neither do they marry nor are they given in marriage, but they are like angels in the heavens.

en.L: For when they rise from [the] dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like angels in the heavens.
en.B: When people rise from the dead, there is no marrying or being given in marriage. They are like the angels in heaven.
en.R: When dead people come back to life, men will not take wives, and women will not be given to husbands. Everyone will be like the angels in heaven.

es.L: Porque cuando resucitan de [los] muertos, ni se casan ni son dados en matrimonio, sino que son como ángeles en los cielos.
es.B: Cuando los muertos resucitan, ya no se casan ni se dan en matrimonio, sino que son como los ángeles en el cielo.
es.R: Cuando los muertos vuelvan a la vida, los hombres no tomarán esposa, ni a las mujeres las darán en matrimonio. Todos serán como los ángeles en el cielo.

sw.L: Kwa maana watakapofufuka kutoka kwa wafu, hawaoi wala hawaozwi, bali wako kama malaika walioko mbinguni.
sw.B: Wafu wanapofufuka, hakuna kuoa wala kuozwa. Wao ni kama malaika walioko mbinguni.
sw.R: Wafu watakaporudi kuwa hai, wanaume hawataoa, na wanawake hawataozwa. Kila mtu atakuwa kama malaika walioko mbinguni.

decisions.choice: marry, be given in marriage: the man took a wife, and a father gave his daughter
alternatives: two words for the same act
decisions.reason: The first verb is used of the man, the second of the woman given in marriage by her family.

decisions.choice: like angels: not dying and not marrying, not turned into angels
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say that people become angels, but that, like them, they no longer marry. Those who do not die need no heirs, so the law of 12:19 no longer applies. The Sadducees were known to deny angels and spirits as well (Acts 23:8).

decisions.choice: the heavens: heaven, where God is
decisions.reason: The plural is a common way of speaking of heaven.

decisions.choice: men will not take wives, and women will not be given to husbands
alternatives: they neither marry nor are given in marriage
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the two verbs.

source.text: περὶ δὲ τῶν νεκρῶν ὅτι ἐγείρονται οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ Μωϋσέως ἐπὶ τοῦ βάτου πῶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς λέγων· Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ;

records.literal_gloss: Concerning now the dead that they are raised, not have you read in the book of Moses at the bush, how spoke to him God saying, I [am] the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob?

en.L: And concerning the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, at [the passage about] the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, 'I [am] the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob'?
en.B: As for the dead being raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God said to him, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?
en.R: Now think about whether the dead are raised. Moses wrote about the time when God spoke to him from a burning bush. You have read that, have you not? God said to Moses, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.'"

es.L: Y acerca de los muertos, que son resucitados, ¿no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} leído en el libro de Moisés, en [el pasaje de] la zarza, cómo Dios le habló, diciendo: “Yo [soy] el Dios de Abraham y el Dios de Isaac y el Dios de Jacob”?
es.B: En cuanto a que los muertos resucitan, ¿no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} leído en el libro de Moisés, en el pasaje de la zarza, cómo Dios le dijo: “Yo soy el Dios de Abraham, el Dios de Isaac y el Dios de Jacob”?
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:piensen|pensad}} si los muertos resucitan. Moisés escribió sobre la vez en que Dios le habló desde una zarza que ardía. {{plural_you:Ustedes han|Vosotros habéis}} leído eso, ¿verdad? Dios le dijo a Moisés: “Yo soy el Dios de Abraham, el Dios de Isaac y el Dios de Jacob”.

sw.L: Na kuhusu wafu, kwamba wanafufuliwa, je, hamjasoma katika kitabu cha Musa, kwenye [habari ya] kichaka, jinsi Mungu alivyomwambia, akisema, 'Mimi [ni] Mungu wa Ibrahimu, na Mungu wa Isaka, na Mungu wa Yakobo'?
sw.B: Na kuhusu wafu kufufuliwa, je, hamjasoma katika kitabu cha Musa, katika habari ya kichaka, jinsi Mungu alivyomwambia, 'Mimi ni Mungu wa Ibrahimu, Mungu wa Isaka, na Mungu wa Yakobo'?
sw.R: Sasa fikirini kama wafu wanafufuliwa. Musa aliandika habari za wakati ule Mungu aliposema naye kutoka katika kichaka kilichokuwa kikiwaka moto. Mmesoma habari hiyo, sivyo? Mungu alimwambia Musa, 'Mimi ni Mungu wa Ibrahimu, Mungu wa Isaka, na Mungu wa Yakobo.'

decisions.choice: I am the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: Exodus 3:6
decisions.reason: God spoke these words to Moses from the burning bush. Jesus argues from the books of Moses, which the Sadducees held in the highest honor.

decisions.choice: at the bush: in the passage about the bush
decisions.reason: Before chapters and verses, a passage could be named by what it told about. "The bush" is the section of Exodus that tells of the burning bush. Mark 2:26 may cite a passage the same way, "in the passage about Abiathar".

decisions.choice: they are raised: God raises them
decisions.reason: The verb is passive. Rising from the dead is God's work, as Jesus has just said (12:24).

en.B: He is not the God of the dead but of the living. How badly you have gone astray!"
en.R: God is not the God of dead people. He is the God of people who are alive. You are very wrong!"

es.L: No es Dios de [los] muertos, sino de [los] vivos. Mucho {{plural_you:se extravían|os extraviáis}}».
es.B: No es el Dios de los muertos, sino de los vivos. ¡Qué lejos {{plural_you:se han extraviado|os habéis extraviado}}!».
es.R: Dios no es el Dios de los muertos. Es el Dios de los que están vivos. ¡{{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} muy equivocados!».

sw.L: Si Mungu wa wafu, bali wa walio hai. Mnapotea sana."
