decisions.choice: not God of the dead but of the living: those God calls his own live to him
alternatives: God is God only of people now living on earth
decisions.reason: God called himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob long after they had died. He would not bind his name to people who had ceased to be. Since he is still their God, they will live, and he will raise them.

decisions.choice: he is not God of the dead, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: he is not the God of the dead
add: you therefore are greatly wrong
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "the" before God, and some add "therefore" to the last sentence. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: greatly going astray: the charge of 12:24 made stronger
decisions.reason: Jesus ends as he began, with the same verb.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God at the start of the sentence.

source.text: Καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς τῶν γραμματέων ἀκούσας αὐτῶν συζητούντων, ἰδὼν ὅτι καλῶς ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς, ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν· Ποία ἐστὶν ἐντολὴ πρώτη πάντων;

records.literal_gloss: And having come up one of the scribes, having heard them debating, seeing that well he answered them, questioned him, Which is commandment first of all?

en.L: And one of the scribes came up, having heard them debating, [and] seeing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had answered them well, he asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Which commandment is first of all?"
en.B: One of the scribes came over and listened to the debate. Seeing that Jesus had answered them well, he put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Of all the commandments, which is first?"
en.R: One of the teachers of God's law came and heard them arguing. He saw that Jesus had answered the Sadducees well. So he asked Jesus, "Which of God's commands is the most important?"

es.L: Y acercándose uno de los escribas, que los había oído discutir, y viendo que les había respondido bien, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Qué mandamiento es [el] primero de todos?».
es.B: Uno de los escribas se acercó y escuchó la discusión. Al ver que Jesús les había respondido bien, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hizo una pregunta: «De todos los mandamientos, ¿cuál es el primero?».
es.R: Uno de los maestros de la ley se acercó y los oyó discutir. Vio que Jesús había respondido bien a los saduceos. Entonces preguntó a Jesús: «¿Cuál de los mandamientos de Dios es el más importante?».

sw.L: Na mmoja wa waandishi akakaribia, akiwa amewasikia wakijadiliana, na akiona kwamba amewajibu vizuri, alimwuliza, "Amri ipi ni ya kwanza kuliko zote?"
sw.B: Mmoja wa waandishi alikuja karibu, akasikiliza mjadala huo. Alipoona kwamba Yesu amewajibu vizuri, akamwuliza swali, "Kati ya amri zote, ipi ni ya kwanza?"
sw.R: Mmoja wa walimu wa sheria alikuja, akawasikia wakibishana. Aliona kwamba Yesu amewajibu Masadukayo vizuri. Basi akamwuliza Yesu, "Ni amri ipi ya Mungu iliyo muhimu kuliko zote?"

decisions.choice: first: first in rank, most important
alternatives: first in order in the law
decisions.reason: The scribe is not asking which command comes first in the books of Moses, but which one ranks above the rest.

decisions.choice: which commandment: a question teachers of the law discussed
decisions.reason: The law held many commands, and later Jewish tradition counted 613. Teachers asked which were weightier. This scribe asks after seeing that Jesus answered well, and 12:32-34 shows he is not trying to trap him.

decisions.choice: seeing, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "knowing that he had answered well" in place of "seeing". The sense is close. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the Sadducees (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who answered and whom, since the scribe is also "he". Readable says "teachers of God's law" for scribes, as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, recorded once in this file: "escribas" is the established Spanish word for these experts in the law; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, recorded once in this file: "waandishi" is the established Swahili word for these experts in the law; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πρώτη ἐστίν· Ἄκουε, Ἰσραήλ, κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστιν, καὶ ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ψυχῆς σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος σου.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus that, First is, Hear, Israel, [the] Lord the God of us [the] Lord one is, \v 30 and you shall love [the] Lord the God of you out of whole the heart of you and out of whole the soul of you and out of whole the mind of you and out of whole the strength of you.

en.L: Jesus answered, "[The] first is, 'Hear, Israel: [the] Lord our God, [the] Lord is one, \v 30 and you shall love [the] Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.'
en.B: Jesus answered, "The first is this: 'Listen, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one. \v 30 And you are to love the Lord your God with your whole heart, your whole soul, your whole mind and your whole strength.'
en.R: Jesus answered, "This is the most important command: 'People of Israel, listen! The Lord our God is the one Lord. \v 30 Love the Lord your God with everything you are. Love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and all your soul. Love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your mind and all your strength.'

es.L: Jesús respondió: «[El] primero es: “Escucha, Israel: [el] Señor nuestro Dios, [el] Señor es uno; \v 30 y amarás [al] Señor tu Dios de todo tu corazón y de toda tu alma y de toda tu mente y de toda tu fuerza”.
es.B: Jesús contestó: «El primero es este: “Escucha, Israel: el Señor nuestro Dios, el Señor es uno. \v 30 Y has de amar al Señor tu Dios con tu corazón entero, con tu alma entera, con tu mente entera y con tu fuerza entera”.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Este es el mandamiento más importante: “¡Pueblo de Israel, escucha! El Señor nuestro Dios es el único Señor. \v 30 Ama al Señor tu Dios con todo lo que eres. Ámalo con todo tu corazón y con toda tu alma. Ámalo con toda tu mente y con todas tus fuerzas”.

sw.L: Yesu alijibu, "[Amri] ya kwanza ni, 'Sikia, Israeli: Bwana Mungu wetu, Bwana ni mmoja; \v 30 na utampenda Bwana Mungu wako kwa moyo wako wote na kwa nafsi yako yote na kwa akili yako yote na kwa nguvu yako yote.'
sw.B: Yesu akajibu, "Ya kwanza ni hii: 'Sikiliza, Israeli: Bwana Mungu wetu, Bwana ni mmoja. \v 30 Utampenda Bwana Mungu wako kwa moyo wako mzima, kwa nafsi yako nzima, kwa akili yako nzima na kwa nguvu yako yote.'
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Amri iliyo muhimu kuliko zote ni hii: 'Ewe Israeli, sikiliza! Bwana Mungu wetu ndiye Bwana pekee. \v 30 Mpende Bwana Mungu wako kwa utu wako wote. Mpende kwa moyo wako wote na kwa nafsi yako yote. Mpende kwa akili yako yote na kwa nguvu yako yote.'

decisions.choice: Hear, Israel: Deuteronomy 6:4-5, the words Israel recited each day
alternatives: a summary in Jesus' own words
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the opening of the prayer later called the Shema, after its first word, "Hear". Faithful Jews said it morning and evening. He adds no command of his own but points to the confession at the heart of the law.

decisions.choice: Lord: in the Hebrew of Deuteronomy, the divine name of God
alternatives: a title of honor for a human master
decisions.reason: Where the Greek has "Lord", the Hebrew text has the divine name. Jews reading aloud said "Lord" in its place, and the Greek Old Testament wrote it that way.

decisions.choice: the Lord our God, the Lord is one: God is one, and there is no other
alternatives: the Lord is our God, the Lord alone
the Lord our God is one Lord
decisions.reason: The words can be grouped in more than one way, and the Hebrew can mean that the Lord alone is Israel's God. The scribe takes it to mean that God is one and there is no other (12:32), and Jesus approves his answer.

decisions.choice: heart, soul, mind and strength: the whole person
alternatives: four separate parts of a person
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy names heart, soul and strength. Mark's form adds mind. Together the words mean love with every part of one's life.

decisions.choice: the first is, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the first of all the commandments is
add at the end: this is the first commandment
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a longer opening, and add after the quotation, "This is the first commandment". The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: The Gospel quotes the Shema in Greek with the word for Lord, so every level writes Lord, as the style for New Testament quotations requires. The meaning note gives the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Love the Lord your God with everything you are, then the four parts in two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable says first what the list means and then breaks it into short sentences, naming God with "him".

decisions.choice: nafsi (soul)
decisions.reason: The soul is a person's inner life, one of four words for the whole person (meaning decision m4). "Roho" is also the word for the Spirit and for breath; "nafsi" keeps the sense of the self, as in Matthew 22:37.

source.text: δευτέρα αὕτη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Second this: You shall love the neighbor of you as yourself.

en.L: [The] second [is] this: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'
en.B: The second is this: 'You are to love your neighbor as yourself.'
en.R: The next most important command is this: 'Love other people as much as you love yourself.'

es.L: [El] segundo [es] este: “Amarás a tu prójimo como a ti mismo”.
es.B: El segundo es este: “Has de amar a tu prójimo como a ti mismo”.
es.R: El segundo mandamiento más importante es este: “Ama a los demás tanto como te amas a ti mismo”.

sw.L: Ya pili [ni] hii: 'Utampenda jirani yako kama wewe mwenyewe.'
sw.B: Ya pili ni hii: 'Mpende jirani yako kama unavyojipenda mwenyewe.'
sw.R: Amri inayofuata kwa umuhimu ni hii: 'Wapende watu wengine kama unavyojipenda wewe mwenyewe.'

decisions.choice: love your neighbor as yourself: Leviticus 19:18
decisions.reason: The command comes from the law of Moses. Jesus sets it next to the command to love God.

decisions.choice: neighbor: the person near, the other person one deals with
alternatives: only the person living next door
decisions.reason: In Leviticus 19:18 the neighbor is a fellow Israelite, and Leviticus 19:34 gives the same command about the foreigner living among them.

decisions.choice: you shall love: a future that gives a command
decisions.reason: As in the law, the future tense states what must be done.

decisions.choice: other people
decisions.reason: Readable avoids a word a young reader may take to mean only the people next door.

source.text: μείζων τούτων ἄλλη ἐντολὴ οὐκ ἔστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Greater than these another commandment not there is.

en.L: There is no other commandment greater than these."
en.B: No other commandment is greater than these two."
en.R: No other command is more important than these two."

es.L: Mayor que estos, otro mandamiento no hay».
es.B: Ningún otro mandamiento es mayor que estos dos».
es.R: No hay ningún otro mandamiento más importante que estos dos».

sw.L: Kuliko hizi, hakuna amri nyingine iliyo kuu zaidi."
sw.B: Hakuna amri nyingine iliyo kuu kuliko hizi mbili."
sw.R: Hakuna amri nyingine iliyo muhimu kuliko hizi mbili."

decisions.choice: these: the two commands together
decisions.reason: The scribe asked for one command; Jesus gives two and holds them together as one answer.

decisions.choice: these two
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that both commands are meant.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ γραμματεύς· Καλῶς, διδάσκαλε, ἐπ’ ἀληθείας εἶπες ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλος πλὴν αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And said to him the scribe, Well, Teacher; on [the basis of] truth you have said that one he is and not there is another besides him;

en.L: And the scribe said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Well [said], Teacher! You have said in truth that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is one, and there is no other besides {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}};
en.B: The scribe said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Well put, Teacher. You have spoken the truth: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is one, and there is no other besides {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The teacher of the law said to Jesus, "That is a good answer, Teacher. What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said is the truth. There is only one God, and there is no other God except {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y el escriba {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¡Bien, Maestro! Con verdad has dicho que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es uno, y no hay otro fuera de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}};
es.B: El escriba {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Bien dicho, Maestro. Has dicho la verdad: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es uno, y no hay otro aparte de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: El maestro de la ley respondió a Jesús: «Esa es una buena respuesta, Maestro. Lo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} dijiste es verdad. Hay un solo Dios, y no hay otro Dios fuera de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Na yule mwandishi akamwambia, "Vema, Mwalimu! Kwa kweli umesema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mmoja, wala hakuna mwingine ila {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}};
sw.B: Yule mwandishi akamwambia, "Umesema vema, Mwalimu. Umesema kweli: {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mmoja, wala hakuna mwingine isipokuwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.
sw.R: Yule mwalimu wa sheria akamwambia Yesu, "Hilo ni jibu zuri, Mwalimu. Ulichosema ni kweli. Kuna Mungu mmoja tu, wala hakuna Mungu mwingine isipokuwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.

decisions.choice: no other besides him: words from Deuteronomy 4:35 and Isaiah 45:21
decisions.reason: The scribe repeats the Shema in words the Scriptures use elsewhere for the one true God.

decisions.choice: he is one, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "God". The earliest manuscripts leave it to be understood. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: well: rightly
decisions.reason: The word praises Jesus' answer as correct.

decisions.choice: There is only one God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the scribe means.

source.text: καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν αὐτὸν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς συνέσεως καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν τὸν πλησίον ὡς ἑαυτὸν περισσότερόν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων καὶ θυσιῶν.

records.literal_gloss: and to love him out of whole the heart and out of whole the understanding and out of whole the strength, and to love the neighbor as oneself, more is than all the whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.

en.L: and to love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all the heart and with all the understanding and with all the strength, and to love the neighbor as oneself, is more than all the whole burnt offerings and sacrifices."
en.B: And to love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all one's heart, all one's understanding and all one's strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is worth far more than every burnt offering and sacrifice."
en.R: People should love God with all their heart, all their understanding and all their strength. And they should love others as much as they love themselves. That matters more than burning animals on the altar or bringing any other sacrifice."

es.L: y el amarlo de todo el corazón y de todo el entendimiento y de toda la fuerza, y el amar al prójimo como a uno mismo, es más que todos los holocaustos y sacrificios».
es.B: Y amarlo con todo el corazón, con todo el entendimiento y con todas las fuerzas, y amar al prójimo como a uno mismo, vale mucho más que todos los holocaustos y sacrificios».
es.R: La gente debe amar a Dios con todo su corazón, con todo su entendimiento y con todas sus fuerzas. Y debe amar a los demás tanto como se ama a sí misma. Eso es más importante que quemar animales sobre el altar o presentar cualquier otro sacrificio».

sw.L: na kumpenda {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kwa moyo wote na kwa ufahamu wote na kwa nguvu zote, na kumpenda jirani kama kujipenda mwenyewe, ni zaidi kuliko sadaka zote za kuteketezwa na dhabihu."
sw.B: Na kumpenda {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kwa moyo wote, kwa ufahamu wote na kwa nguvu zote, na kumpenda jirani kama mtu anavyojipenda mwenyewe, ni bora kupita sadaka zote za kuteketezwa na dhabihu zote."
sw.R: Watu wanapaswa kumpenda Mungu kwa moyo wao wote, kwa ufahamu wao wote na kwa nguvu zao zote. Tena wanapaswa kuwapenda wengine kama wanavyojipenda wenyewe. Hilo ni muhimu zaidi kuliko kuchoma wanyama madhabahuni au kutoa dhabihu nyingine yoyote."

decisions.choice: more than burnt offerings and sacrifices: the teaching of 1 Samuel 15:22 and Hosea 6:6
decisions.reason: The prophets taught that God wants obedience and love more than sacrifice. The scribe says this in the temple courts, where the offerings were made.

decisions.choice: whole burnt offerings: animals burned whole on the altar
decisions.reason: In a whole burnt offering the entire animal was given to God. Sacrifices is the wider word for offerings.

decisions.choice: understanding: the mind, the power to grasp
decisions.reason: The scribe uses a different word from Jesus' "mind" and does not name the soul.

decisions.choice: heart, understanding and strength, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: add: and with all the soul
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and with all the soul", matching 12:30. The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: one's (B); God, People should, That matters more (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the words apply to anyone. Readable names God, makes the rule a statement about people, and says what burnt offerings were.

decisions.choice: holocaustos
decisions.reason: The whole burnt offerings were animals burned whole on the altar (meaning decision m2). "Holocausto" is the Spanish word for that sacrifice; Readable says what it was, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ὅτι νουνεχῶς ἀπεκρίθη εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐ μακρὰν εἶ ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus, having seen him that wisely he answered, said to him, Not far are you from the kingdom of God.

en.L: And Jesus, seeing that he had answered wisely, said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God."
en.B: Jesus saw that he had answered with insight, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God."
en.R: Jesus saw that the man had given a wise answer. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him, "You are close to entering God's kingdom."

es.L: Y Jesús, viendo que había respondido sabiamente, le dijo: «No estás lejos del reino de Dios».
es.B: Jesús vio que había respondido con inteligencia, y le dijo: «No estás lejos del reino de Dios».
es.R: Jesús vio que el hombre había dado una respuesta sabia. Entonces le dijo: «Estás cerca de entrar en el reino de Dios».

sw.L: Na Yesu, alipoona kwamba amejibu kwa busara, alimwambia, "Hauko mbali na ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.B: Yesu alipoona kwamba amejibu kwa hekima, akamwambia, "Hauko mbali na ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.R: Yesu aliona kwamba mtu huyo ametoa jibu la busara. Kwa hiyo akamwambia, "Uko karibu kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu."

decisions.choice: wisely: with good sense and understanding
decisions.reason: The word is used only here in the New Testament. It praises an answer that shows real understanding.

decisions.choice: not far from the kingdom: near, but not yet in
decisions.reason: Jesus praises the man and also leaves something unsaid. Mark does not tell what was still lacking.

decisions.choice: close to entering God's kingdom
alternatives: not far from the kingdom of God
decisions.reason: Readable states the saying positively and says that it is about entering the kingdom.

decisions.choice: el reino de Dios
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, recorded once in this file. Readable keeps the phrase and adds "entrar", as the English Readable does (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: ufalme wa Mungu
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, recorded once in this file. Readable keeps the phrase and adds "kuingia", as the English Readable does (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς οὐκέτι ἐτόλμα αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And no one no longer dared him to question.

en.L: And no one any longer dared to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: After that, no one had the courage to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} anything more.
en.R: After that, no one was brave enough to ask Jesus any more questions.

es.L: Y nadie se atrevía ya a preguntarle.
es.B: Después de eso, nadie tuvo valor para hacerle más preguntas.
es.R: Después de eso, nadie se animó a hacerle más preguntas a Jesús.

sw.L: Na hakuna mtu aliyethubutu tena kumwuliza.
sw.B: Baada ya hapo, hakuna aliyekuwa na ujasiri wa kumwuliza swali lolote zaidi.
sw.R: Baada ya hapo, hakuna mtu aliyethubutu kumwuliza Yesu maswali zaidi.

decisions.choice: no one dared: the end of the questions that began in 11:27
decisions.reason: Two negatives make the statement firm. The leaders, the Pharisees and Herodians, the Sadducees and the scribe have all questioned him. Now Jesus asks the question (12:35).

decisions.choice: After that
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the end of the series.

source.text: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν διδάσκων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· Πῶς λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι ὁ χριστὸς υἱὸς Δαυίδ ἐστιν;

records.literal_gloss: And answering Jesus was saying, teaching in the temple, How say the scribes that the Christ son of David is?

en.L: And answering, Jesus was saying while teaching in the temple, "How [is it that] the scribes say that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is [the] son of David?
en.B: As Jesus was teaching in the temple, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took up the matter: "How can the scribes say that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is the son of David?
en.R: Jesus was teaching in the temple courtyard. He asked, "Why do the teachers of God's law say that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is the son of King David?

es.L: Y respondiendo, Jesús decía, mientras enseñaba en el templo: «¿Cómo [es que] dicen los escribas que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} es hijo de David?
es.B: Mientras enseñaba en el templo, Jesús planteó la cuestión: «¿Cómo pueden decir los escribas que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} es hijo de David?
es.R: Jesús estaba enseñando en el patio del templo. Preguntó: «¿Por qué dicen los maestros de la ley que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} es hijo del rey David?

sw.L: Na Yesu, akijibu, alikuwa akisema, alipokuwa akifundisha hekaluni, "Waandishi husemaje kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mwana wa Daudi?
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa akifundisha hekaluni, aliliendeleza jambo hilo: "Waandishi wanawezaje kusema kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mwana wa Daudi?
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa akifundisha katika ua wa hekalu. Akauliza, "Kwa nini walimu wa sheria wanasema kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mwana wa Mfalme Daudi?

decisions.choice: answering: taking up the matter, not replying to a question
decisions.reason: No one has asked anything (12:34). The word marks Jesus' response to the debates he has heard.

decisions.choice: the Christ is the son of David: the promised king of David's line
alternatives: a teaching of the scribes only
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16; Isaiah 11:1). Bartimaeus called Jesus Son of David (10:47-48), and the crowd hailed the coming kingdom of David (11:10).

decisions.choice: the temple: its courts
decisions.reason: Jesus taught in the open courts around the sanctuary, as in 11:27.

decisions.choice: took up the matter (B); King David (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of "answering" here. Readable says who David was.

source.text: αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ εἶπεν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ· Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου.

records.literal_gloss: Himself David said by the Spirit the Holy, Said [the] Lord to the Lord of me, Sit at [the] right [hand] of me until I put the enemies of you under the feet of you.

en.L: David himself said by the Holy Spirit, '[The] Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right [hand] until I put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet."'
en.B: David himself, speaking by the Holy Spirit, said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Take {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} seat at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand, until I put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies beneath {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet."'
en.R: David himself spoke by the power of the Holy Spirit. He said, 'The Lord God said to my Lord, "Sit beside {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right, in the place of honor. Stay there until I defeat all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies."'

es.L: David mismo dijo en el Espíritu Santo: “Dijo [el] Señor a mi Señor: ‘Siéntate a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha, hasta que ponga a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} enemigos debajo de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} pies’”.
es.B: David mismo, hablando por el Espíritu Santo, dijo: “El Señor dijo a mi Señor: ‘Toma asiento a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha, hasta que yo ponga a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} enemigos bajo {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} pies’”.
es.R: David mismo habló por el poder del Espíritu Santo. Dijo: “El Señor Dios le dijo a mi Señor: ‘Siéntate junto a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha, en el lugar de honor. Quédate allí hasta que yo derrote a todos {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} enemigos’”.

sw.L: Daudi mwenyewe alisema katika Roho Mtakatifu, 'Bwana alimwambia Bwana wangu, "Keti upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mpaka niwaweke adui {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} chini ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}."'
sw.B: Daudi mwenyewe, akinena kwa Roho Mtakatifu, alisema, 'Bwana alimwambia Bwana wangu, "Kaa kitini upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} hadi nitakapowaweka adui {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} chini ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}."'
sw.R: Daudi mwenyewe alisema kwa nguvu ya Roho Mtakatifu. Alisema, 'Bwana Mungu alimwambia Bwana wangu, "Keti karibu {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, mahali pa heshima. Kaa hapo mpaka nitakapowashinda adui {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} wote."'

decisions.choice: the Lord said to my Lord: Psalm 110:1
decisions.reason: The psalm is headed "of David". God invites David's lord, the king, to sit beside him while God subdues his enemies.

decisions.choice: two Lords: in the Hebrew, the divine name, and then "my lord"
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew psalm the first "Lord" is the divine name, and the second is a word for a human master or king. David speaks of someone greater than himself as "my lord".

decisions.choice: sit at my right hand; under your feet: the place of highest honor and power, and full victory
alternatives: a seat beside a host at a meal
decisions.reason: The right hand of a king was the place of honor and shared rule. A king set his feet on defeated enemies (Joshua 10:24).

decisions.choice: under your feet, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "a footstool for your feet", as in the Greek of the psalm and in Luke 20:43. The SBLGNT reads "under your feet". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: by the Holy Spirit: speaking as one inspired by God
decisions.reason: Jesus treats the psalm as David's words, given by the Spirit, and so as true.

decisions.choice: Lord ... Lord
decisions.reason: The Gospel quotes the psalm in Greek, where both words are "Lord", and Jesus' argument rests on that. Every level writes Lord, and the meaning note gives the Hebrew. Readable adds "God" to the first Lord.

decisions.choice: in the place of honor; until I defeat all your enemies
alternatives: at my right hand; under your feet
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two pictures.

decisions.choice: upande wa kulia wangu
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of "at the right (hand)", recorded once in this file: the plain word for the right side, the place of highest honor (meaning decision m3). "Mkono wa kuume" is older and less familiar to many readers.

source.text: αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ λέγει αὐτὸν κύριον, καὶ πόθεν αὐτοῦ ἐστιν υἱός;

records.literal_gloss: Himself David calls him Lord, and from where of him is he son?

en.L: David himself calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Lord, and how is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} his son?"
en.B: David himself calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Lord. How then is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} his son?"
en.R: David himself calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} 'Lord.' So in what way is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} David's son?"

es.L: David mismo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llama Señor; ¿y cómo es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hijo suyo?».
es.B: David mismo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llama Señor. Entonces, ¿cómo puede ser su hijo?».
es.R: David mismo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llama “Señor”. Entonces, ¿en qué sentido es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hijo de David?».

sw.L: Daudi mwenyewe anamwita Bwana, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwana wake jinsi gani?"
sw.B: Daudi mwenyewe anamwita Bwana. Basi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anawezaje kuwa mwana wake?"
sw.R: Daudi mwenyewe anamwita 'Bwana.' Basi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwana wa Daudi kwa namna gani?"

decisions.choice: how is he his son: the Messiah is more than a son of David
alternatives: the Messiah is not descended from David
decisions.reason: A father did not call his son "lord". Jesus does not deny that the Messiah is David's son; Mark has already called Jesus Son of David (10:47-48). The question shows that the Messiah is also David's Lord. Jesus leaves his hearers to draw the conclusion.

decisions.choice: from where: how, in what sense
decisions.reason: The question word asks for the source or ground of a claim.

decisions.choice: David's
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear whose son is meant.

source.text: καὶ ὁ πολὺς ὄχλος ἤκουεν αὐτοῦ ἡδέως.

records.literal_gloss: And the large crowd was hearing him gladly.

en.L: And the large crowd was listening to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} gladly.
en.B: The great crowd listened to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with delight.
en.R: The large crowd enjoyed listening to Jesus.

es.L: Y la gran multitud {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escuchaba con agrado.
es.B: La gran multitud {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escuchaba con deleite.
es.R: A la gran multitud le gustaba escuchar a Jesús.

sw.L: Na umati mkubwa ulikuwa ukimsikiliza kwa furaha.
sw.B: Umati mkubwa wa watu ulimsikiliza kwa furaha.
sw.R: Umati mkubwa wa watu ulifurahia kumsikiliza Yesu.

decisions.choice: the large crowd: the great number of people present
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean the great crowd or the mass of ordinary people, as opposed to the leaders. Either way the people stand in contrast to the scribes Jesus warns about next.

decisions.choice: was listening: the tense pictures continued listening
decisions.reason: They kept on listening with pleasure.

source.text: Καὶ ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν· Βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων ἐν στολαῖς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις, οἱ κατεσθίοντες τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσευχόμενοι· οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα.

records.literal_gloss: And in the teaching of him he was saying, Beware of the scribes, those wanting in robes to walk about and greetings in the marketplaces \v 39 and first seats in the synagogues and first places at the dinners, \v 40 those devouring the houses of the widows and for a pretext at length praying; these will receive greater judgment.

en.L: And in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying, "Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes, and [like] greetings in the marketplaces \v 39 and the first seats in the synagogues and the first places at the dinners, \v 40 who devour the houses of widows and for a pretext pray at length. These will receive greater condemnation."
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Keep clear of the scribes. They love to parade about in long robes and to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces. \v 39 They want the front seats in the synagogues and the best couches at banquets. \v 40 They eat up the property of widows, and for show they pray on and on. Their sentence will be all the heavier."
en.R: Jesus kept teaching. He said, "Be careful about the teachers of God's law. They like to go around in long robes that show how important they are. They like people to greet them with honor in the market places. \v 39 They want the most important seats in the synagogues. At big dinners they want the places where the honored guests sit. \v 40 They cheat widows and take away their homes. And they say long prayers so that people will think they are good. God will punish them more than others."

es.L: Y en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza decía: «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado con los escribas, que quieren andar con túnicas largas, y [quieren] saludos en los mercados, \v 39 y los primeros asientos en las sinagogas y los primeros lugares en los banquetes; \v 40 los que devoran las casas de las viudas y, como pretexto, oran largamente. Estos recibirán mayor condena».
es.B: Mientras enseñaba, decía: «{{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}} de los escribas. Les encanta pasearse con túnicas largas y que los saluden con respeto en los mercados. \v 39 Quieren los asientos de delante en las sinagogas y los mejores lugares en los banquetes. \v 40 Se comen los bienes de las viudas, y para aparentar hacen oraciones interminables. Su condena será todavía más severa».
es.R: Jesús siguió enseñando. Dijo: «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado con los maestros de la ley. Les gusta andar con túnicas largas que muestran lo importantes que son. Les gusta que la gente los salude con honor en los mercados. \v 39 Quieren los asientos más importantes en las sinagogas. En las grandes cenas quieren los lugares de los invitados de honor. \v 40 Engañan a las viudas y les quitan sus casas. Y hacen oraciones largas para que la gente piense que son buenos. Dios los castigará más que a otros».

sw.L: Na katika mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} alikuwa akisema, "Jilindeni na waandishi, wanaotaka kutembeatembea wakiwa na mavazi marefu, na [kutaka] salamu katika viwanja vya soko, \v 39 na viti vya kwanza katika masinagogi na nafasi za kwanza katika karamu; \v 40 wao wanaomeza nyumba za wajane, na kwa kisingizio wanaomba kwa muda mrefu. Hawa watapokea hukumu iliyo nzito zaidi."
sw.B: Alipokuwa akifundisha, alisema, "Jiepusheni na waandishi. Wanapenda kuzunguka wakiwa wamevaa majoho marefu, na kusalimiwa kwa heshima sokoni. \v 39 Wanataka viti vya mbele katika masinagogi na nafasi bora katika karamu. \v 40 Wanatafuna mali za wajane, na kwa maonyesho wanaomba maombi marefu. Adhabu yao itakuwa nzito zaidi."
sw.R: Yesu aliendelea kufundisha. Alisema, "Kuweni waangalifu na walimu wa sheria. Wanapenda kutembea wakiwa wamevaa majoho marefu yanayoonyesha jinsi walivyo watu muhimu. Wanapenda watu wawasalimu kwa heshima sokoni. \v 39 Wanataka viti muhimu kuliko vyote katika masinagogi. Kwenye karamu kubwa wanataka kukaa mahali wanapoketi wageni wa heshima. \v 40 Wanawadanganya wajane na kuwanyang'anya nyumba zao. Tena wanasali sala ndefu ili watu wadhani kwamba wao ni watu wema. Mungu atawaadhibu zaidi kuliko wengine."

decisions.choice: long robes: the flowing garments that marked men of rank and learning
decisions.reason: Scribes wore long robes that set them apart as learned men worthy of honor.

decisions.choice: first seats, first places: the seats of honor in the synagogue and at a meal
decisions.reason: In the synagogue the leading seats faced the people. At a feast guests reclined on couches, and the places nearest the host were for the most honored (Luke 14:7-10).

decisions.choice: devour the houses of widows: consume the property of widows
decisions.reason: A house here means a household's goods and living. Mark does not say how they did it. Scribes could act as trustees of an estate or take gifts from the devout, and either could be abused. The law forbade wronging widows (Exodus 22:22).

decisions.choice: for a pretext pray at length: long prayers made for show or as a cover
decisions.reason: The word means a pretense or false front. Their long prayers win them trust and honor, and hide what they do.

decisions.choice: greater judgment: a heavier sentence from God
decisions.reason: Those who use religion to rob the weak will be judged more severely than others, because God defends widows (Deuteronomy 10:18).

decisions.choice: who like ... who devour: a description of the scribes Jesus warns against
decisions.reason: The clauses describe the scribes he has in mind. Jesus has just praised one scribe (12:34), so the warning is about the conduct, not about every scribe.

decisions.choice: that show how important they are; cheat widows and take away their homes; God will punish them
alternatives: in long robes; devour the houses of widows; will receive greater judgment
decisions.reason: Readable explains the robes, the picture of devouring houses, and who will judge them.

decisions.choice: devoran las casas (L); se comen los bienes (B)
decisions.reason: "Devour the houses of widows" means consuming their property (meaning decision m3, uncertain). Literal keeps the picture; Balanced says "bienes", as the English Balanced says "property", and keeps the verb of eating.

decisions.choice: wanaomeza nyumba (L); wanatafuna mali (B)
decisions.reason: "Devour the houses of widows" means consuming their property (meaning decision m3, uncertain). Literal keeps the picture with "kumeza" (to swallow); Balanced says "mali" (property), as the English Balanced does, and keeps a verb of eating.

source.text: Καὶ καθίσας κατέναντι τοῦ γαζοφυλακίου ἐθεώρει πῶς ὁ ὄχλος βάλλει χαλκὸν εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον· καὶ πολλοὶ πλούσιοι ἔβαλλον πολλά·

records.literal_gloss: And having sat down opposite the treasury he was watching how the crowd casts money into the treasury; and many rich were casting much.

en.L: And sitting down opposite the treasury, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was watching how the crowd puts money into the treasury; and many rich people were putting in much.
en.B: Jesus sat down across from the offering boxes and watched the crowd dropping their money into them. Many rich people were giving large sums.
en.R: Jesus sat down near the place where people gave money to the temple. He watched the crowd putting their money into the offering boxes. Many rich people put in a lot of money.

es.L: Y sentándose frente al tesoro, observaba cómo la multitud echa dinero en el tesoro; y muchos ricos echaban mucho.
es.B: Jesús se sentó frente a las cajas de las ofrendas y observaba cómo la gente echaba su dinero en ellas. Muchos ricos daban grandes sumas.
es.R: Jesús se sentó cerca del lugar donde la gente daba dinero para el templo. Miraba cómo la gente echaba su dinero en las cajas de las ofrendas. Muchos ricos echaban mucho dinero.

sw.L: Na akiwa ameketi mkabala wa hazina, alikuwa akitazama jinsi umati unavyotia fedha katika hazina; na matajiri wengi walikuwa wakitia [fedha] nyingi.
sw.B: Yesu aliketi mkabala wa masanduku ya sadaka, akawatazama watu wakitumbukiza fedha zao humo. Matajiri wengi walikuwa wakitoa kiasi kikubwa.
sw.R: Yesu aliketi karibu na mahali ambapo watu walitoa fedha kwa ajili ya hekalu. Aliutazama umati ukitia fedha katika masanduku ya sadaka. Matajiri wengi walitia fedha nyingi.

decisions.choice: the treasury: the offering chests in the temple courts
decisions.reason: The word can mean a treasure room, but here people put money into it in sight of others. Later Jewish writings describe thirteen chests shaped like trumpets set out in the temple courts for gifts.

decisions.choice: money: copper coins, small change
decisions.reason: The word means copper, and so the copper coins of everyday use.

decisions.choice: puts: present tense in what Jesus watched
decisions.reason: Jesus watched the giving as it went on.

decisions.choice: offering boxes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the treasury was.

decisions.choice: el tesoro (L); las cajas de las ofrendas (B, R)
decisions.reason: The treasury here is the offering chests in the temple courts (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say what they were, as the English "offering boxes" does; Literal keeps the Greek word's sense, "treasury". The same in verse 43.

decisions.choice: hazina (L); masanduku ya sadaka (B, R)
decisions.reason: The treasury here is the offering chests in the temple courts (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say what they were, as the English "offering boxes" does; Literal keeps the Greek word's sense, "treasury". The same in verse 43.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθοῦσα μία χήρα πτωχὴ ἔβαλεν λεπτὰ δύο, ὅ ἐστιν κοδράντης.

records.literal_gloss: And having come one widow poor cast two lepta, which is a quadrans.

en.L: And one poor widow came and put in two lepta, which is a quadrans.
en.B: Then a poor widow came and dropped in {{units:two little copper coins, worth a few minutes' wages|two lepta, which make a quadrans}}.
en.R: Then a widow who was very poor came. She put in {{units:two tiny copper coins that were worth almost nothing|two lepta, which make a quadrans}}.

es.L: Y viniendo una viuda pobre, echó dos leptones, que es un cuadrante.
es.B: Entonces llegó una viuda pobre y echó {{units:dos moneditas de cobre, que valían el salario de unos pocos minutos|dos leptones, que hacen un cuadrante}}.
es.R: Luego llegó una viuda muy pobre. Echó {{units:dos monedas de cobre muy pequeñas que casi no valían nada|dos leptones, que hacen un cuadrante}}.

sw.L: Na mjane mmoja maskini akaja, akatia lepta mbili, yaani kodranti moja.
sw.B: Kisha akaja mjane mmoja maskini, akatumbukiza {{units:sarafu mbili ndogo za shaba, zenye thamani ya mshahara wa dakika chache|lepta mbili, ambazo ni kodranti moja}}.
sw.R: Kisha mjane mmoja aliyekuwa maskini sana alikuja. Alitia {{units:sarafu mbili ndogo kabisa za shaba ambazo thamani yake ilikuwa ndogo mno|lepta mbili, ambazo ni kodranti moja}}.

decisions.choice: two lepta, which is a quadrans: the smallest coins, together a sixty-fourth of a denarius
decisions.reason: The lepton was the smallest copper coin in use. Mark explains its worth by a Roman coin, the quadrans, which was a quarter of the as. Sixty-four of them made a denarius, a day's wage (12:15).

decisions.choice: a poor widow: a woman with no husband to support her, and in want
decisions.reason: Widows were among the most helpless people in Israel. She is one of those Jesus has just said the scribes devour (12:40).

decisions.choice: two little copper coins, worth a few minutes' wages (B); two tiny copper coins that were worth almost nothing (R); the coin names as the original units
alternatives: two lepta, which is a quadrans
decisions.reason: The units setting gives the value of the coins by default and their names as the alternative. Literal keeps the coins.

decisions.choice: {{units:dos moneditas de cobre, que valían el salario de unos pocos minutos|dos leptones, que hacen un cuadrante}}
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable say what the smallest coins were worth (meaning decision m1), with the coin names as the alternative, "leptones" and "cuadrante" in their Spanish forms. Literal keeps the coins.

decisions.choice: {{units:sarafu mbili ndogo za shaba, zenye thamani ya mshahara wa dakika chache|lepta mbili, ambazo ni kodranti moja}}
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable say what the smallest coins were worth (meaning decision m1), with the coin names "lepta" and "kodranti" as the alternative. Literal keeps the coins; "senti" would put a modern currency in the story.

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν τῶν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον·

records.literal_gloss: And having called to [him] the disciples of him he said to them, Truly I say to you that the widow this the poor more than all has cast of those casting into the treasury;

en.L: And calling {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Truly I say to you that this poor widow has put in more than all those putting [money] into the treasury.
en.B: He called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples over and said to them, "Truly I tell you, this widow, poor as she is, has given more than all the others who are giving to the offering boxes.
en.R: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "I tell you the truth: this poor widow gave more than all the other people who put money in the offering boxes.

es.L: Y llamando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, les dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que esta viuda pobre ha echado más que todos los que echan en el tesoro.

records.literal_gloss: All for out of the abounding to them cast, but she out of the poverty of her all as much as she had cast, whole the living of her.

en.L: For they all put in out of what they had in abundance, but she out of her want put in all that she had, her whole living."
en.B: The others all gave from what they had left over. But she, in her need, gave everything she had, the whole of what she had to live on."
en.R: The others gave money they did not need. But she is very poor, and she gave all the money she had. She gave what she needed to live on."

decisions.choice: her whole living: all her means of life
decisions.reason: The word can mean life, but here it means the means of living, the money she needed for food and shelter.

decisions.choice: abundance, want: what is left over, and what is lacking
decisions.reason: The rich gave from their surplus. She gave from what she lacked.

decisions.choice: she gave everything: praise for her devotion, and perhaps a lament
alternatives: only praise for her generous gift
only a protest against the temple taking her last coins
decisions.reason: Jesus contrasts her whole-hearted gift with the rich. Mark sets the story right after the warning about scribes who devour widows' houses (12:40) and right before Jesus foretells the temple's ruin (13:1-2). So her gift may also show how the system took everything from the poor. The text does not say which Jesus meant, and both may be in view.

decisions.choice: money they did not need
alternatives: out of what they had in abundance
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what giving from abundance means.
